items.caption:
Sam Altman hopes AI finds a candidate to cure or treat a major disease within the next couple of years.

He is careful about the timeline: the FDA process will take a while, so this is about discovering a candidate that still has to go through testing, not a cure on shelves.

Would you trust a drug discovered by AI?

Source: Matthew Berman (Forward Future), Sam Altman: RSI, AI Consciousness, OpenAI's New Hardware, Compute, and more! Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=3gXLmy7DK_4

items.caption:
Sam Altman says people were wrong about AI killing the need for coders.

Six to twelve months ago, many were certain of it. His lesson: the world actually had demand for way more software than anyone thought.

Is AI creating more coding work or less where you are?

items.caption:
Sam Altman says he hasn't read or even looked at a line of code in probably a year.

He doesn't code for work, but used to write small personal projects for fun. Now he doesn't think he'll ever do that again.

When did you last write code by hand?
